messages:
alex_support: FYI customer Concord (prod) reporting p99 jump after we flipped concord-v2 yesterday. Long-context requests (>8k) are timing out or returning 502. Auth errors intermittently. Escalating to runtime + ml.

sre-bot: Alert: model=concord-v2 p95 170ms -> 640ms, p99 220ms -> 3.2s, error-rate increased 0.2% -> 2.9% (since 1719790000). Incident auto-created.

maya_eng: Can you paste a minimal repro request + headers? Which route?

alex_support: Repro posted by customer 10:22 UTC: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'x-api-model: concord-v2' -d '{"input": "<~10k token document>", "max_tokens":512}'

jordan_ml: Noted. Concord-v2 includes a new BPE-normalizer patch (merge-optim) that alters token boundaries for CJK + long whitespace sequences. That can increase number of tokens and break our prefix-KV hit heuristics -> more cache misses.

tali_runtime: Also seeing spikes in auth-proxy latency -> some requests hit a 502, falling back to synchronous CPU path in the runtime which adds ~1.2-2.7s. Logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T10:21:17Z] auth-proxy: upstream 502 for conn=2345 user=concord-prod
[2026-03-15T10:21:17Z] router: fallback_to_cpu inference_id=abc123 model=concord-v2
[2026-03-15T10:21:17Z] runtime: cpu_sync_exec latency=1800ms tokens_out=450
```

anya_sre: Do we have traces showing where time is spent? prefix vs kv vs model-compile?

alex_support: Attaching trace snippet from customer request (sanitized): 
```
span 0: http receive 12ms
span 1: auth-proxy 312ms (502 transient)
span 2: router decision 4ms
span 3: runtime kv-cache lookup 25ms (miss)
span 4: model infer (cpu fallback) 2100ms
span 5: streaming flush 10ms
```

jordan_ml: kv-cache misses on longctx are suspicious. The tokenizer change increases token count at boundary which pushes past our cached prefix length (4k tokens) more often. Also concord-v2's fused attention kernel is tuned for quantized weights; fallback CPU path never hits those kernels.

maya_eng: Immediate mitigation options?

jordan_ml: Short-term: add a routing rule that rejects/redirects concord-v2 for requests with estimated input_tokens > 6k (based on content-length heuristic) and route to concord-v1. Medium: pin existing dedicated customers to concord-v1 until we fix tokenizer. Long: revert tokenizer normalization or release an updated tokenizer that preserves token counts.

tali_runtime: We can also force non-fallback path: patch auth-proxy to retry upstream auth (small window) instead of letting router fall back to CPU. Patch risk is low but needs rollout.

billing-bot: Heads-up: customer reported duplicate retries which doubled billed tokens for the failing requests. Recommend issuing a pro-rated credit if we confirm double-charge.

customer_ops: Customer note: "We started seeing timeouts right after the update. Some calls succeed but many error with 502 and the product latency is unusable for >8k docs."

alex_support: Action items: 1) maya -> run repro on canary with tracing and full headers. 2) jordan -> prepare pin-v1 routing rule + rollback plan for tokenizer. 3) tali -> quick auth-proxy retry patch + deploy to canary. 4) anya -> monitor p99 and error-rate; throttle concord-v2 for free-tier traffic to reduce blast. 5) billing-bot -> flag customers for credits.

maya_eng: Running the repro now on canary with env VAR USE_KVCACHE=true and TRACE=1: `./local_repro.sh --model concord-v2 --input sample_longctx.json`

sre-bot: Incident INC-2026-042 created and assigned to eng-runtime. Priority=P1.

anya_sre: I'm going to add a temporary routing rule to deprioritize concord-v2 for long-context requests (will set weight=0.1) and watch p99 for 15m.

jordan_ml: I built a tokenizer fallback that forces concord-v2 to use byte-level tokenization for >6k chars. Will push to canary if the auth-proxy patch reduces spurious fallbacks.

tali_runtime: Rolling out auth-proxy small retry (2 retries, 50ms backoff) to canary now. If green, will extend.

billing-bot: Noted affected customer list; creating credit tickets for those with >2x token billing in the window 1719780000-1719870000.

alex_support: Thanks — please update thread with timelines. I'll ping customer with interim mitigation (pin them to concord-v1) and offer credit. :handshake:

maya_eng: Canary repro confirms: when auth-proxy returns 502 we see fallback to CPU and p99 jumps to ~2.1s. With the retry patch canary, the auth 502s drop and p99 for concord-v2 longctx falls to ~420ms (still above concord-v1 baseline).

jordan_ml: Given canary, plan: rollback tokenizer normalization from concord-v2 -> concord-v2a (maintain other perf improvements) by 17:30 UTC. Will coordinate with runtime for cache warm-up.

anya_sre: I'm leaving the temporary routing rule for 1h then re-evaluate. If p99 doesn't recover we will roll to concord-v1 globally for longctx.

alex_support: Summaries for customer: 1) we applied routing throttle to reduce exposure, 2) auth-proxy retry reduced fallbacks, 3) we will rollback the tokenizer change and follow up on credits. Will update SLA ticket.

customer_ops: Customer replied: "Appreciate the quick response. Please confirm when we are fully on concord-v1 or when the tokenizer fix is live."

alex_support: Assigning owners and ETA: jordan -> tokenizer rollback by 17:30 UTC; tali -> auth-proxy patch to prod after canary validation (ETA 16:45 UTC); anya -> monitor & revert routing rule (ongoing); maya -> close repro and attach traces to incident.

jordan_ml: I'll post the rollback PR link in 10m.

sre-bot: Update: auth-proxy canary shows 90% reduction in 502s; p99 improved. Incident status: investigating -> mitigation in progress.

alex_support: Thanks team. Will follow up with customer once rollback PR merges. :white_check_mark:
